<description>
While reviewing #36642 I found something else we missed in JSON-RPC 2.0:

If we receive a malformed request we would assume that we couldn't parse it's jsonrpc version and send an HTTP error.  This is how the legacy jsonrpc server worked (despite that behavior not ever being part of any ratified jsonrpc spec) and we maintain it as Bitcoin "legacy" jsonrpc protocol. However it's possible to form a request that does properly indicate jsonrpc 2.0 but is still malformed. In that case, we should not send an HTTP error: the correct protocol is to respond with `HTTP 200 OK` and include the jsonrpc error message in the response.

The solution is to check if we know the request's jsonrpc version before responding with an error.

We already correctly handle such malformed requests in batches and this is already tested in `test_batch_requests()` in `interface_rpc.py`

On master, the functional test in this PR actually crashes the node because the assumption is codified. Note that this crash requires:
1. RPC Authentication
2. A debug build

So this is not an urgent security fix, but a bug that might disrupt testing.

```
node0 stderr httprpc.cpp:46
    UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue, const JSONRPCRequest &, HTTPStatusCode &):
        'jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2' check failed.
```

In release builds the node doesn't crash, but it returns HTTP 400 with a JSON-RPC 2.0 error body instead of HTTP 200.
</description>

[2026-11-16] rc:4589017331 inline on src/httprpc.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-16):
In commit "rpc: requests that fail to parse can not be jsonrpc2.0 notifications" (7f7428b457ed2a3394dfc0e626485aaac4dbc266)

I suggested adding this block in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4498229560, but I think it should be dropped, because it's dead code in this PR. `IsNotification()` is only true after `parse()` succeeds, and nothing that throws after a successful parse reaches `JSONErrorReply()`: a single 2.0 request runs with [`catch_errors=true`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/7f7428b457ed2a3394dfc0e626485aaac4dbc266/src/rpc/server.cpp#L725-L732), the whitelist check returns 403 without throwing, and batch elements catch their own errors. Adding this dead code also makes it harder to understand how the real change in this commit actually works.

(I included this in my earlier suggestion because I was mixing this PR up with #36753, which needs something similar when it refuses a valid notification after parsing. But it can just be added there, so `JSONErrorReply` does not need to change at all in this commit.)
[2026-11-16] r:5923710074 review APPROVED by ryanofsky (member):
Code review ACK 7f7428b457ed2a3394dfc0e626485aaac4dbc266. On master, a malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 request makes debug builds abort and gets an HTTP 400 in release builds. With this PR it gets an HTTP 200 reply with the error, as the spec requires, and invalid requests without an id now get an error reply instead of being treated as notifications, both alone and in batches.

Since the last review, the only changes are the new commit messages and the two test cleanups. Thanks for taking these! One more suggestion, not a blocker: the [`HTTP_NO_CONTENT` branch in `JSONErrorReply()`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4589017331) that I suggested earlier turns out to be dead code, and could be dropped from the last commit.
